artboards.title: The whole thing — every screen, every tap
The year — one tap from home
One week — one tap from the year
The job verdict, logged in place
A lane, and the goal open on it
A why, and what it used to say

annotations.text:
WATERSHED — LOCKED FOR THE PROTOTYPE.

Nine screens, and nothing on this canvas that is not one of them. The boards we argued past — the horizontal home, the button-first home, the lane picker as its own screen, the two-ribbon year, the three doors, the unfolded wall — are out of the design and kept only in git.

ROW ONE is the loop: open, log, and back to where you started.
ROW TWO is the only other thing the app does: change resolution.
ROW THREE is what hangs off the record, plus the locked encoding.

If a screen is not in one of those rows, it is not in the prototype.

THE LOOP — OPEN, LOG, BACK. Two taps, and the same screen at both ends.

1. HOME, DAY UNANSWERED. The day's question and four lane names. No log button: the lanes are the answer. Nothing is singled out and no sentence is pushed at you.
2. THE LANE, AND THE GRID. Your own words at the top because you chose this lane, six cells at the bottom in thumb reach. Size across, enlarged or diminished down. One tap writes the block.
3. HOME, DAY ANSWERED. The same home screen with the question gone, because it has been answered. Three weeks of marks, the job ribbon beside them, ADD ANOTHER at the foot — which reopens screen 1 and closes the loop.

HOME IS ONE SCREEN IN TWO STATES, not two screens. That is the whole trick: you are asked once a day and only until you answer, so the question can never become a nag.

One thing to know before building: NOTHING, IT WAS THE JOB answers the day without writing a block. So an answered day is not proof that anything was logged, and the door's absence is not a receipt.

HOME TO THE YEAR — IT IS A RESOLUTION, NOT A DESTINATION.

The record's header carries the scale: 3 WEEKS / THE YEAR, the live one underlined. One tap changes resolution, one tap changes it back. There is no year 'section', no tab bar, no menu — the year is the same rails, in the same order, with the same encoding, drawn at eleven pixels a row instead of twenty-five.

That is why the encoding had to hold at both resolutions: footprint means size, fill means enlarged, fade means diminished, whether the unit is a day or a week. The year is legible for free because nothing new was invented for it.

AND BACK DOWN AGAIN. A year is for noticing, not for reading — the March turn in the job, the eight months with no BODY. When something in it catches you, tap that week and you get the seven days at full size. That is the only drill-down in the app, and it exists so a year can be asked a question rather than just admired.

So: HOME -> THE YEAR is one tap. THE YEAR -> A WEEK is one tap. A WEEK -> BACK is one tap. Nothing here is more than one tap from the record.

WHAT ELSE HANGS OFF THE RECORD. Three things, each one tap away, each returning to it.

THE JOB VERDICT. Tap today's cell in the ribbon and three cells open in place: enlarged, diminished, no work. No size — the job's is always the same and you already know it. No screen, because a full screen for one bit of information reads as a chore.

A LANE, AND ITS GOAL. Tap a lane name. The spine: why the lane exists, the goal currently open on it, and the blocks it has earned. Time accumulated, never time remaining.

A WHY, AND WHAT IT USED TO SAY. One step further in. A changed why is an event, not an edit: old versions struck through and dated, keeping the blocks they earned.

THE TEST FOR WHETHER SOMETHING IS A LANE: could it go quiet for six weeks without you noticing?

If yes, it is a lane — the silence is the finding, and the rail is how you see it.
If no, it is not. The job cannot silently go quiet; you would be unemployed. Drawing fifty-two identical fat bars for it is decoration, not information.

And on overlap: one lane per block, and the choosing IS the reflective act. But that only survives contact with real life if the moment of hesitation is rare. A good lane set is one where roughly nine blocks in ten are obvious and the tenth makes you think for two seconds. If every block is ambiguous, the lanes are wrong — not the rule.

Four lanes here, down from six. MONEY is gone: Cadence already does it, and a lane that duplicates a tool you already use produces no surprise. THE JOB is gone as a lane — see the variant below. What remains are the four that can go quiet on you.

Four rails, 81px each. Fewer lanes means bigger marks, more air, and a year view you can actually read.

THE VALUE IS AT WRITE TIME, NOT READ TIME.

Every habit tracker puts its value at read time: log dutifully all year, get a chart. The logging is a tax you pay for the chart, which is why it degrades into bookkeeping inside a fortnight.

If Hollis is right that you know in the body within a second, then the tap is not data entry — it is a two-second somatic check on time you have already spent. That is the product. The year view is the receipt.

Three screens follow from taking that seriously. D puts your own sentence between you and the mechanics, so the pause lands on the reason rather than on the UI. E makes a changed why an event rather than an edit, because 'you find out when you read it and flinch' is only true if the flinch is recorded. F is the one that has to stay empty: the block joins the rail and nothing else happens, with the four things that did not happen listed underneath so that the silence reads as a decision.

B — THE YEAR, DECIDED.

The job is drawn the way a lane is drawn: one bar a week, the same length every time, with only the solid/faded split moving. One encoding rule, not two.

The day-grain version — five 4px marks a week — was drawn beside this one and dropped. At 11px a row it turns to dither: you can see the year darken, but no week says anything and the texture competes with the lanes.

The blank rows are the one week off in August, drawn by nothing.

LOCKED. B FULL / FADED for the day mark, 1 STACKED for the week cell.

One rule holds at both resolutions: footprint means size, fill means enlarged, fade means diminished. Rejected options kept and dimmed — a decision without its reasons is just a preference.

A — HOW YOU LOG A VERDICT.

No screen and no prompt: the ribbon cell IS the control. Tap today's cell and three cells open in place under the row; tap one and it closes. Two taps, no navigation, and the day grid never leaves the screen.

This is deliberately not the 3x2 grid. There is no size to pick, so a full screen for one bit of information would read as a chore — which is exactly how a daily ask turns into a streak you resent.

NO WORK is the third cell rather than a default, because a day off is a real answer and the app should never guess it from the calendar.

Skip a day and the cell stays blank. Nothing counts it, nothing mentions it, and no badge appears.
